subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required for host filesystem, exec/session, slash-command, CLI, and cron toolCall access?
rationale: The unresolved surfaces can expose privileged process, filesystem, session, Gateway, cron, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK and command cron sufficient for now, and reject broader host-FS, exec, slash-command, CLI, and generic cron dispatch until a sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is primarily about dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundaries, where this person has the strongest recent history.
